This question from @gregsargent.bsky.social doesn't seem that hard to me. 

When progressives relentlessly attack moderate Democrats as corrupt, that undermines the moderate message that Trump's corruption is a huge deal.

I am supportive of all these independent plays, but given the ninety-seven layers of coordination-without-coordinating it requires to pay off I really think it would be simpler to just broaden the tent and bring back Democrats with Baucus/Landrieu/Nelson-style ideologies.

Dems should continue to invest in MI-Sen and WI-Gov even if AES & Hong are the nominees, but ME-2 as an open seat with a progressive factionalist candidate just doesn’t make sense as a target district. This whole fiasco Dunlap put into motion was 100% predictable and shameful.
Hunter the only one to remember that it was progressives not moderates who wanted his dad to stay on the ticket even after the debate!
Everyone says Democrats can’t just be anti-Trump but it seems like “orange man bad” is a much more broadly appealing message than anything else you could come up with.

What if the bold, forward-thinking agenda was:

1. Reverse the specific things Trump has done to make life less affordable (tariffs, SNAP/Medicaid cuts) 

2. Block and investigate Trump’s corruption 

Do you, in fact, need to stand for more than that?

This is why Anita Earls is on the Slow Boring donation recommendation list — moderate Dems can and do win statewide in North Carolina but we need to flip to Supreme Court to break the extreme gerrymander that’s made a joke of NC democracy.
